about.title: Trips, planned and followed in one place
about.description: Dalefy is a trip companion app. Travel organisers build itineraries in a shared workspace, and travellers follow their trip live on their phone.

sections.heading: For travel organisers
sections.html:
Dalefy is the workspace where a travel team plans a trip end to end.

  • Build day-by-day itineraries with flights, stays, transfers and events.
  • Import bookings and confirmations, with flight details checked automatically.
  • Manage travellers, documents and compliance for each trip.
  • Publish the finished itinerary to travellers with your own branding, by email, link or in the app.

sections.heading: For travellers
sections.html:
Travellers use the Dalefy app on iPhone and Android to follow the trip their organiser planned.

  • See the full itinerary, updated live if plans change.
  • Get flight status, reminders for what's next, and a home screen widget counting down to departure.
  • Keep trip documents, maps and the shared photo gallery in one place.

sections.heading: Signing in
sections.html:
Dalefy is used by travel organisations and their clients. Access to the organiser workspace is by invitation from your team admin. Travellers join a trip from the link or PIN their organiser sends them.

Sign in with Google, Apple or your email address. We only use your account to confirm who you are. See the privacy policy for what we store.

changelog.title: What's new
changelog.description: Recent changes across the Dalefy app and workspace. App updates arrive automatically; the App Store version number is shown under Profile, then About.

releases.heading: Dale gets live answers, and you can report a photo
items: Dale can answer with live flight status and the weather where you're going, and shows the events it's talking about as cards you can tap.
Dale asks before it sends anything to the AI for the first time. The privacy policy now names Anthropic, the company behind it.
Report a photo someone else added to the gallery. It's hidden for you straight away and your organiser is told so they can review it.
Transfers show the meeting point, the driver and their phone number. Event times show in 24-hour.
Android: sheets, cards and the Dale message box are solid instead of see-through, and the keyboard no longer covers what you type.

releases.heading: Trip info and your organiser's photo
items: Trip info reads like a document, and phone numbers, emails and links are tappable everywhere.
Your organiser's photo appears on the trip, and traveller photos show across the itinerary.
Where you're staying always shows, even when the itinerary didn't list it separately.

releases.heading: Today before, during and after your trip
items: Today shows your hotel before you go, tonight's stay while you travel and a photo recap once you're home.
Messages from your organiser arrive in the notifications list, even when you opened the app from the lock screen.
Leave a trip by pressing and holding it on Home.
Documents open inside the app, and the first tap after opening the app is faster.

releases.heading: Meet Dale
items: Dale is the trip assistant. Ask about your flights, hotels, meals or what's on tomorrow, and it answers from your itinerary and your organiser's notes.
Find it under Ask Dale on Home and on the trip page.

releases.heading: A quicker start and faster updates
items: A new first screen: sign in or enter your trip code in one box, and a short tour of the app built from your own trip.
Changes from your organiser reach your phone as soon as they're published, instead of every 30 seconds.
Flight alerts check every 15 minutes around departure, and only notify you about changes you need to act on.
Map pins stay in the trip's own country and cities.

releases.heading: A new look for the app
items: Home and Today redesigned, with frosted sheets, a day strip and a countdown on each trip.
New flight and event pages: a ticket in the airline's colours, photo headers and smoother moves between events.
Join a trip has PIN and Scan tabs, shows a big preview of the trip, and accepts a pasted link.
Trip links and QR codes open straight into the app.
Widgets and Live Activities redesigned, and notifications show the trip photo with quick actions.
The Gallery groups photos under a banner for each trip and keeps the date each photo was taken.

releases.heading: Branded email, and widgets that land on the right day
items: Team invitations, sign-in links, verification and password reset emails now arrive on Dalefy's own design instead of a generic template.
Itinerary updates reach travellers without the app by email, alongside the push notification for those who have it.
The home screen widget and Live Activities open the trip page scrolled to that day.

releases.heading: Mobile polish and stability
items: Cover photos blend into the page instead of stopping in a hard line, on both light and dark themes.
Fixed the gallery stuttering, an app that hung when opened offline, and sections that stayed invisible on Home and Today.
The photo viewer is lighter and opens without a jump.

releases.heading: dalefy.app
items: Dalefy moved to dalefy.app. Links and emails now use the new address.
PDF exports carry the organiser's logo, and flight rows use clearer icons.
The app starts faster and the notification sheet is quieter.

releases.heading: Widgets and Live Activities
items: A home screen widget counts down to your next trip and shows what's next once you are travelling.
Flight progress and the next event can appear on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island.
Travellers now only receive the events assigned to them.

releases.heading: Accounts, legal pages and the tab bar
items: Sign in with Apple and Google use the official marks, and you can delete your account from Profile.
Privacy policy, terms and support pages published.
The tab bar tucks away as you scroll, and Today is a single scrolling page.

releases.heading: New Home and Trip design
items: Home and Trip screens redesigned with a photo hero, inset cards and a timeline with category icons.
Every event has a category with its own colour and icon, on mobile, web and the shared itinerary.
Dashboard rebuilt around the next trip, upcoming flights and traveller invites.

releases.heading: Design parity
items: Reports, Travellers, Media, Destinations and Dashboard brought onto one visual system.
Destinations globe is interactive.

support.title: Help & support
support.description: Answers to the common questions, and how to reach us when you need a person.

sections.heading: Contact us
sections.html:
Email support@dalefy.app and we will get back to you as soon as we can. If your question is about a booking, a hotel or a flight, your trip organiser is usually the fastest route, and their details are on the trip's Info page.

It helps if you include your app version. You will find it in the app under Profile, then About, then Version. Tap it to copy it.

faqs.question: How do I join a trip?
faqs.answer: Tap the plus button on the Home tab and enter the six-digit PIN your organiser sent you. You can also scan the QR code or paste the invite link from the same screen.

faqs.question: Where is my itinerary?
faqs.answer: Open your trip from Home. Today shows what is coming up next, and the trip page shows every day in order. Tap any event for the details, tickets and documents your organiser attached.

faqs.question: What does the home screen widget do?
faqs.answer: It counts down to your next trip and, once you are travelling, shows what is next. Tap it to open that day in the app. Add it from your phone's widget gallery.

faqs.question: Can I add photos?
faqs.answer: Yes. Open the Gallery tab and tap the plus button to add photos or videos from your camera roll. Everyone on the trip can see what is shared there.

faqs.question: Can I report a photo?
faqs.answer: Yes. Open the photo in the Gallery and tap the flag, or press and hold it and choose Report. It's hidden for you straight away, and your organiser is told so they can review it and remove it.

faqs.question: What is Dale?
faqs.answer: Dale is the trip assistant. Tap Ask Dale on Home or on the trip page and ask anything about your trip, like when your next flight is or which meals are included. It answers from your itinerary and your organiser's notes, and can check live flight status and the weather.

faqs.question: Can I rely on Dale's answers?
faqs.answer: Dale uses AI, so it can get things wrong. For anything that matters, like a flight time or a meeting point, check the event itself or ask your organiser.

faqs.question: What does Dale send to the AI?
faqs.answer: Your question and your trip's details, including the names of people on the trip, go to Anthropic's Claude AI to write the answer. They aren't used to train it. Dale asks before it's used for the first time. More in the privacy policy.

faqs.question: How do I leave a trip?
faqs.answer: On Home, press and hold the trip and choose Leave Trip. It comes off your phone and your organiser's list. You'll need the PIN or link to join again.

faqs.question: Do I need an account?
faqs.answer: No. You can join and use a trip without one. Signing in with Apple, Google or an email link keeps your trips with you if you change phones. Go to Profile, then Sign in.

faqs.question: I asked for a sign-in link but nothing arrived
faqs.answer: Check your spam folder for an email from team@dalefy.app. Links work once and expire after an hour, so request a fresh one if it has been a while.

faqs.question: How do notifications work?
faqs.answer: Trip reminders arrive before each event, and itinerary updates and messages arrive when your organiser sends them. Everything also stays in the list behind the bell on Home. If you have not installed the app, updates come by email instead. Both can be turned off under Profile, then Notifications.

faqs.question: What is Live Activity?
faqs.answer: On iPhone, flight progress can show on your lock screen and in the Dynamic Island while you travel. Turn it off under Profile, then Notifications if you would rather not see it.

faqs.question: How do I delete my account?
faqs.answer: Go to Profile and tap Delete account below Sign out. The full steps are on the delete your account page.

faqs.question: How do I get access to the workspace?
faqs.answer: Ask your team admin to invite you from Settings, then Team. You will receive an email with a sign-in link that also accepts the invitation.

faqs.question: How do travellers get the itinerary?
faqs.answer: From a trip, use Send to email a branded itinerary with the trip link and PIN, or copy the link and PIN to share however you like. Travellers can view it on the web or in the app.

faqs.question: Will travellers see changes I make?
faqs.answer: Yes. The shared link is live. Travellers with the app get a push notification, and travellers without it get an email summarising what changed.

faqs.question: Can I use my own branding?
faqs.answer: Set your company name, logo and accent colour under Settings, then Branding. They appear on the shared itinerary, the app screens for your trips, and the emails Dalefy sends on your behalf.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What Dalefy collects, why, and how to get it removed.

sections.heading: Who we are
sections.html: Dalefy is a trip companion app. Travel organisers publish itineraries to it, and travellers use it to follow their trip. When a trip is branded "Powered by" an organiser, that organiser planned the trip, and Dalefy provides the app.

sections.heading: What we collect
sections.html:
If you sign in: your name, email address and profile photo, as provided by Apple, Google or the email link you used. Signing in is optional for travellers.

Trip data: the trips you join, the traveller you link yourself to on a trip, and the photos and videos you add to a trip gallery.

Details your organiser adds: an organiser can record a traveller's phone number, date of birth, nationality, dietary needs, emergency contact and notes so they can run the trip. These are kept in the organiser's workspace, are seen only by the organiser's team, and are not shown to other travellers. Dalefy never stores passport details.

App activity: when you last opened a trip and whether you use iPhone or Android, so your organiser can see who has the latest plan.

Reports: if you report a photo, we keep the report and tell your organiser which photo it was and who reported it.

Device data: a random identifier for this installation so your trips stay with the device, and a push notification token if you allow notifications. On iPhone, a Live Activity token lets flight progress show on your lock screen.

Location: the app does not track where you are. Event addresses set by your organiser are looked up on a map so the app can show them to you.

Cookies: the website uses no tracking or advertising cookies. It stores a sign-in session and your theme choice in your browser, and nothing else.

sections.heading: How we use it
sections.html:
• To show you your trips, and keep them in sync across your devices when you are signed in.
  • To send trip reminders and itinerary updates you have opted into, by push notification or email.
  • To send sign-in links, verification and password reset emails when you ask for them.
  • To share your name and avatar with the other people on the same trip.
  • To answer the questions you ask Dale, the trip assistant in the app, and to help organisers import and edit itineraries.
  • To let organisers review photos that have been reported, and remove them.
  • To answer support requests you send us.

We do not sell your personal information, and we do not use it for advertising.

sections.heading: Who we share it with
sections.html:
• Your trip organiser can see who has joined their trip, which traveller you linked to, when you last opened it, and any photo reports you make.
  • Google Firebase stores accounts, trip data and uploaded media, and delivers push notifications.
  • Resend delivers the emails Dalefy sends, such as itineraries, invitations and sign-in links.
  • Mapbox provides maps and looks up the event addresses on a trip.
  • Apple and Google handle sign-in when you choose them, and Apple handles Live Activities.
  • Expo routes push notifications and app updates to your device.
  • AeroDataBox provides live flight status. It receives flight numbers and dates, not your name.
  • OpenWeather provides the weather for the places on a trip. It receives place coordinates only.
  • Vercel hosts the website and the services behind the app.
  • Anthropic provides the Claude AI behind Dale and the organiser's itinerary tools. When you ask Dale something, your question and your trip's details, including the names of people on the trip, are sent to Anthropic to write the answer. The app asks before Dale is used for the first time. Anthropic doesn't use this data to train its models.

All of this data travels over encrypted connections. Each provider only receives what it needs for its job.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
sections.html: Trip data stays for as long as the trip exists with the organiser. Your account and profile stay until you delete them. Photos you add to a gallery stay with that trip until you or the organiser remove them. Email delivery records are kept by our email provider for a short period for troubleshooting.

sections.heading: Deleting your data
sections.html:
In the app, go to Profile and tap Delete account. That removes your profile, your trip memberships and your avatar, and signs you out. Photos you added to a trip gallery can be removed from the gallery itself.

You can also email support@dalefy.app from the address on your account and we will do it for you. The full steps are on the delete your account page.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.html: Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, export or erase the personal data we hold about you, and to object to certain uses. Email us and we will respond within 30 days. If you are in the UK or EU you can also complain to your data protection authority.

sections.heading: Children
sections.html: Dalefy is not aimed at children under 16. Younger travellers on a family or group trip are added by their organiser, who is responsible for having the right consent.

sections.heading: Changes and contact
sections.html: If this policy changes in a way that matters, we will update the date above and note it on the what's new page. Questions go to support@dalefy.app.

summary: Signing in is optional for travellers. If you do, we keep your name, email address and profile photo.
Your organiser sees who joined their trip. The other people on the trip see your name and avatar.
We never store passport details, and we don't sell your data or use it for advertising.
You can delete your account at any time from Profile in the app.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.description: The short version: be a good guest, and remember your organiser runs the trip.

sections.heading: Agreeing to these terms
sections.html: By using the Dalefy app or website you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use Dalefy.

sections.heading: Organisers and travellers
sections.html:
Dalefy is the app. The trip itself is planned and run by a travel organiser, who publishes the itinerary, times, bookings and documents you see. When a trip is branded "Powered by" a company, that company is your organiser.

Dalefy is not a travel agent, carrier or hotel, and is not a party to any booking. Your contract for flights, accommodation and activities is with your organiser or the provider. Times and details can change, so check with your organiser or the carrier before you travel.

sections.heading: Who can use Dalefy
sections.html: You must be at least 16 to create an account. Younger travellers can be added to a trip by their organiser with the consent of a parent or guardian.

sections.heading: Your account
sections.html: Signing in is optional for travellers. If you do sign in, keep your sign-in method secure and tell us if you think someone else has used it. Sign-in links and invitations we email you are personal to you and work once. You can delete your account at any time from the Profile tab.

sections.heading: Organiser workspaces
sections.html: Organiser accounts belong to a team. Team admins decide who is invited, what role they hold and when access ends. Organisers are responsible for the accuracy of the itineraries they publish and for having the right to share the traveller details and documents they upload.

sections.heading: Your content
sections.html:
You own the photos, videos and text you add to a trip. By adding them to a shared gallery you allow the other people on that trip, and your organiser, to see them in the app. Dalefy does not claim ownership of your content.

Only add content you have the right to share. Do not add anything illegal, harmful, abusive, or that infringes someone else's rights. Organisers and Dalefy can remove content that breaks these terms.

There is no tolerance for objectionable content or abusive users. If you see something that breaks these terms, report it from the photo. It is hidden for you straight away and your organiser is asked to review it. Organisers and Dalefy can remove the content and the account of whoever posted it.

sections.heading: Using the service fairly
sections.html:
• Do not share trip PINs, QR codes or invite links with people who are not on the trip.
  • Do not try to access trips, accounts or data that are not yours.
  • Do not interfere with the app, its servers or other people's use of it.
  • Do not use Dalefy to send unsolicited messages or emails.

sections.heading: Dale, the trip assistant
sections.html: Dale answers questions about your trip using AI, from the itinerary and notes your organiser published. AI can make mistakes, so Dale's answers are a guide, not a confirmation. Check important times, places and bookings in the trip itself or with your organiser.

sections.heading: Availability
sections.html: We work hard to keep Dalefy available, but we cannot promise it will always be online or error free. We may change, pause or retire features at any time. Keep a copy of anything critical, such as tickets, outside the app.

sections.heading: Liability
sections.html: Dalefy is provided "as is". To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for loss or damage arising from your use of the app, including missed connections, changed bookings or lost data. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited by law.

sections.heading: Ending your use
sections.html: You can stop using Dalefy and delete your account whenever you like. We may suspend or end access for anyone who breaks these terms.

sections.heading: Law and changes
sections.html:
These terms are governed by the laws of England and Wales. If we change them in a way that matters, we will update the date above and let you know in the app.

Questions go to support@dalefy.app.

summary: Dalefy is the app. Your organiser plans and runs the trip, and your bookings are with them or the provider.
You own the photos and text you add. Only add what you have the right to share.
Keep trip PINs and invite links to the people on the trip.
Dale's answers are a guide. Check important times in the trip or with your organiser.
You can stop using Dalefy and delete your account whenever you like.

delete-account.title: Delete your account
delete-account.description: How to remove your Dalefy account and the data that goes with it.

sections.heading: In the app
sections.html:
1. Open the Profile tab.
  2. Scroll to the bottom and tap Delete account, below Sign out.
  3. Confirm. If you signed in with Apple or Google you may be asked to sign in again first, which is a security check.

Deletion is immediate and signs you out on that device.

sections.heading: By email
sections.html: If you no longer have the app, or you would rather we did it, email support@dalefy.app from the address on your account with the subject "Delete my account". We will confirm and complete it within 30 days.

sections.heading: What gets deleted
sections.html:
• Your profile: name, email address and avatar.
  • Your sign-in method with Apple, Google or email.
  • Your memberships of every trip you joined, and the traveller link on each.
  • Your push notification and Live Activity tokens.

sections.heading: What stays
sections.html:
• Photos and videos you added to a shared trip gallery. Remove them from the gallery before you delete if you do not want them to stay with the trip.
  • The trip itself, which belongs to the organiser who planned it. Your name may still appear on the organiser's traveller list, as that is their record of who they took on the trip.
  • Records our providers keep for a short period for security and troubleshooting, such as email delivery logs.

sections.heading: Organiser accounts
sections.html: If you are part of an organiser team, ask your team admin to remove you from the team first under Settings, then Team. Then delete your account the same way, or email us. Trips you created stay with the team.
